title: Field Deployment: Capacity, Security and Hardware Readiness Profile
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This document defines a field-ready deployment readiness profile for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) customers. It collects concrete, testable "minimum" and "recommended" requirements across compute, storage, network, security integrations (KMS, HSM), and telemetry so field engineers, SREs, and customer success can validate a site prior to handoff. The checklist is intended for pre-installation validation, acceptance tests during initial install, and as a reference for upgrades and hardware replacements.

Goals

- Provide a single checklist that is actionable for on-site engineers and customer IT teams.
- Reduce rework during field installs by surfacing incompatibilities early (firmware, drivers, MTU, BGP templates).
- Define measurable acceptance tests (commands, thresholds, and telemetry signals).

Scope

This profile covers:
- Bare metal and VM hosts used for Redwood inference nodes (CUDA/GPU and CPU-only pools).
- Network topology and vendor-neutral routing and firewall expectations.
- Storage sizing and performance targets for model artifacts, KV- and prefix-caching, and local scratch.
- Key management and certificate/profile expectations for KMS integration, certificate rotation, and HSM requirements.
- Telemetry, logging and alert endpoints required for post-install monitoring and capacity planning.

Not in scope: detailed playbooks for product-specific upgrades (those live in upgrade-and-rollback).

Minimum hardware profile (pass/fail for initial acceptance)

| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Acceptance Criteria | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| GPU node SKU | 1 x A10 / A16 or equivalent (16GB) | 2 x A100 40GB (recommended for production inference) | GPUs visible via nvidia-smi, driver satsified (see driver section) | For small test clusters only; production should use >= 2x A100 or equivalent NVML capacity |
| CPU-only node | 16 vCPU, 64 GB RAM | 48 vCPU, 256 GB RAM | lscpu shows cores, top/htop stable under load | CPU nodes used for control plane, queuing, metrics ingestion |
| Local storage | 500 GB NVMe (persistent) | 2 TB NVMe (RAID1 if necessary) | fio random-read 128k: p95 latency <= 2 ms at sustained 300 MB/s | Fast local NVMe for model weights and KV cache |
| Network | 1 Gbps management + 10 Gbps service NICs | Dual 25 Gbps with SR-IOV | iperf3 throughput within 10% advertised; MTU 9000 when using jumbo frames | Ensure low jitter for p95 token latency |
| Control-plane nodes | 3 nodes, 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM | 3 nodes, 8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM | API handshake success <100ms on internal network | HA quorum required |
| KMS/HSM | Accessible KMS endpoint over TLS; service account with encrypt/decrypt keys | HSM or cloud KMS with dedicated HSM slot | Key wrap/unwrap tested; certificate chain validates | See KMS section for policies |

Driver, kernel and OS expectations

- Supported OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (preferred), RHEL 8.6+ (supported).
- Kernel: 5.15+ for Ubuntu 22.04; RHEL with tuned kernel errata applied.
- NVIDIA driver: 535.x or later for Ampere support. Verify with: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv
- CUDA: 11.8+ where GPU nodes are required.
- Container runtime: containerd 1.6+ or Docker 20.10+ (containerd preferred).
- Recommended sysctl adjustments:
  - net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
  - vm.swappiness=10
  - fs.file-max >= 524288
- Hugepages: not strictly required, but document whether enabled; if enabled, confirm setup with: cat /proc/meminfo | grep HugePages

Network architecture and configuration patterns

- Topology: Separate networks for management, data plane (inference), and telemetry. Where possible, dedicate a NIC per plane.
- MTU: Preferred 9000 for data plane. Validate: ip link set dev <iface> mtu 9000; ip link show <iface> | grep mtu
- Routing: BGP is preferred for multi-rack failover. Provide the BGP template we use (example below).
- Firewall: Allow ports: 443 (control plane), 9090 (metrics pipeline), 50051 (gRPC between runtime nodes), 6379 (redis if deployed), 22 (SSH for field eng). Restrict to known management CIDRs.

Example BGP config template (customer to fill local-AS / neighbor):

router bgp CUSTOMER_AS
  neighbor REDWOOD_PEER remote-as 65021
  neighbor REDWOOD_PEER description "Redwood control plane"
  network 10.0.0.0/24

Storage topology and tuning

- Local NVMe used for model artifacts and KV cache; networked object store (S3 compatible) required for long-term model storage.
- Recommended filesystem: ext4 with noatime for local NVMe; mount options: noatime,nodiratime,barrier=1.
- Example fio workload for acceptance: fio --name=nvme-read --rw=randread --bs=128k --size=10G --numjobs=4 --runtime=60 --time_based --group_reporting
- Acceptance thresholds: p95 read latency <= 2ms; sustained throughput >= 300 MB/s per NVMe under load.

KMS and secrets integration

- Redwood requires an endpoint for envelope encryption. Supported KMS: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM with PKCS#11.
- Policy: Redwood will perform envelope encryption; customer must provide a key with encrypt/decrypt and generateDataKey permissions.
- Acceptance steps:
  1) Confirm network egress and TLS to KMS endpoint: curl -v https://kms.example.com/health
  2) Key wrap test: use provided test harness to perform GenerateDataKey / Encrypt / Decrypt cycle.
  3) Observe key rotation window and provide rotation schedule to Redwood.

Telemetry and observability requirements

- Required endpoints:
  - Metrics (Prometheus pull) on port 9090 (internal and optionally scraped by Redwood aggregator).
  - Traces (OTLP/OTel) via HTTP/GRPC to configured collector.
  - Logs: central logging (syslog/rsyslog -> collector) or Filebeat shipping to aggregator.
- Sampling and retention: initial pilot should send 1x traffic at full QPS to validate volume.
- Minimum labels and tags required on metrics: cluster_id, rack_id, node_role, gpu_model, tenant_id.
- Example prometheus scrape config snippet:
  - job_name: 'redwood-nodes'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['10.1.2.3:9090']

Operational acceptance tests (run during handoff)

1. Node inventory verification (pass/fail)
   - Run: inventory.sh --summary (provided in field-tools). Expected: GPUs, NICs, NVMe devices listed match customer manifest.
2. Network baseline test
   - Run iperf3 between two service NICs for 60s at expected MTU. Pass if throughput >=90% of link rate and packet loss <0.1%.
3. Storage performance test
   - Run fio workload above. Pass if p95 latency and throughput meet thresholds.
4. KMS handshake and key wrap test
   - Run sample key operations. Pass if round-trip completes and wrapped keys decrypt.
5. Control plane API validation
   - curl --cacert <ca.pem> https://control-plane.internal/v1/health -> expect 200 OK and JSON {"status":"ok"} within 500ms.
6. Inference smoke test
   - Deploy a canary model and send 100 concurrent small requests (<=64 tokens). Pass if p95 token latency < 250ms, error rate < 1%.

Procedures for common field issues

- Driver mismatch (GPU nodes fail to register):
  1) Collect: dmesg, nvidia-smi, kubectl describe node (if k8s).
  2) Action: Reinstall driver matching supported list; reboot host.
  3) If persistent, revert to known-good driver image provided in releases archive.
- High storage latency discovered after install:
  1) Confirm thermal throttling on NVMe (smartctl).
  2) Check IO scheduler and filesystem mount options.
  3) If hardware faulty, replace NVMe and rehydrate from object store.
- KMS connectivity intermittent:
  1) Validate TLS chain and proxy settings.
  2) Temporarily switch to offline key (pre-wrapped key in secure vault) per emergency policy. Notify security owner.

Ownership and contact matrix

- Field install lead: Customer Escalations (owner: customer-success).
- SRE escalation: eng-sre@redwood.example.com.
- KMS/security: security@redwood.example.com.
- Telecom/networking questions: infra-networking@redwood.example.com.

Rollout constraints and capacity planning guidance

- Minimum cluster size for production inference (p95 token latency SLAs): 4 GPU nodes with autoscale headroom of 50% for bursty traffic.
- Recommended headroom policy: configure autoscaler to maintain 20% idle GPU capacity for cold-start sensitive workloads.
- If using mixed-GPU types, validate model quantization fallback is enabled to allow CPU fallback for critical traffic.

Acceptance signoff artifact checklist

- Completed inventory sheet (CSV) with serial numbers and firmware versions.
- FIO and iperf3 run logs attached.
- KMS test logs and key IDs used for envelope test.
- Canary inference run logs (latency and error rates).
- Prometheus target list and sample metrics (30 minutes of data).
- Handoff email with runbook and emergency contact list.

Appendix: quick commands and scripts

- Verify GPUs: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv
- Basic NVMe check: lsblk -d -o name,rota,model,size; smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
- Iperf3 example: iperf3 -c 10.1.2.4 -t 60 -P 8 -f m
- Fio example: fio --name=nvme-read --rw=randread --bs=128k --size=10G --numjobs=4 --runtime=60 --time_based

Revision history

- 2026-01-12: Draft created by Ava Martinez.
- 2026-02-10: Reviewed and validated with field team; added KMS acceptance steps and updated GPU driver version.

If you find discrepancies between this profile and customer manifest, escalate to eng-private-deployments triage with full inventory and test logs attached.
